votes.evidence:
Worktree /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215 (PR #75215 head a7fb363bef6; receivers.py and stamphog tasks.py are in the PR's file list).

Mechanics the finding describes are accurate as far as they go: products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:125-138 registers one on_commit per qualifying save, _start_stamphog_review (receivers.py:210-235) calls queue_inbox_pr_review which does process_inbox_pr_review.delay (products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:147-155), and the worker fetches the PR (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1158-1167) before the head-keyed select_for_update dedupe (tasks.py:1203-1222).

Reachability in production, however, is narrow and bounded:
- Gate: stamphog_review_inbox_prs defaults False (products/review_hog/backend/models.py:294, db_default=False). Only opted-in reviewers' signal-report implementation runs dispatch at all; receivers.py:96-111 further requires signal_report_id, non-internal task.
- Refire volume: the receiver drops every save whose update_fields excludes "output" without a DB hit (receivers.py:87-90). In products/tasks/backend, the only output-touching saves are set_task_run_output (facade/api.py:2154, the agent server's one-shot "PR opened" write; it preserves pr_url on merge), update_task_run PATCH with an output dict (facade/api.py:2060-2075), and the webhook's _record_run_output_field (webhooks.py:276-299), which is idempotent per key: pr_url written once (webhooks.py:212) and pr_merged once (webhooks.py:235). The pr_merged refire costs one GET and exits at tasks.py:1168-1171 because state != "open". All other tasks-side saves use update_fields=["state", ...] (5 sites) and never reach the dispatch. Net: a handful of GET /pulls/N per PR against a GitHub App installation budget, not "many".
- Rate-limit pressure is handled: GitHubRateLimitError is caught and retried with countdown >= 60s (tasks.py:1160-1162).
- Deliberate, documented tradeoff: receivers.py:76-80 ("a same-head re-trigger costs one fetch (early-exit)") and tasks.py:1157 ("The fetch runs before the dedupe because the dedupe keys on the PR's current head, which only GitHub knows"). The suggested dispatch-time key on "last processed PR URL" would suppress the lost-synchronize recovery path the PR explicitly tests: products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py:992 case "missed_webhook_head_gets_reviewed" and "failed_run_recreated_on_refire".
votes.refutation: The claim that repeated output saves "can create many broker messages and GitHub requests" has no reachable production trigger at that scale: the toggle is opt-in and default off, the tasks backend writes output for a PR-bearing run only a few times per lifetime (one agent-server pr_url write, one idempotent webhook pr_url backstop, one idempotent pr_merged write that early-exits after a single GET), and every other save is state-only and filtered before any work. Each refire costs exactly one Celery message and one GET, and rate-limit responses back off. The pre-dedupe fetch is an acknowledged design choice: dedupe must key on the PR's current head sha, which only GitHub can supply, and the finding's suggested dispatch-time dedupe on PR URL would break the tested recovery cases (missed webhook head, failed run recreation). This is a bounded, intentional tradeoff, not a defect. A short cache cooldown keyed on (task_run_id, pr_url) could shave the rare duplicate GET, but nothing in the code shows a load problem that warrants it.
